I’m 69 years old, and I’ve been working these fields in Quzhou County since I was a teenager. I finished middle school, so I can read the numbers on fertilizer bags and I listen when the extension agent comes by, but I don’t trust anything until I’ve seen it work with my own eyes or heard about it from my neighbors. I farm about 6 mu of land all together. This year, I’m keeping 4 mu in the wheat-maize double crop—that’s been the backbone of my family’s food and income for decades—and I’m planting 2 mu of cotton. I thought about dropping the cotton because my back isn’t what it used to be and the picking is hard on my wife and me, but the cotton money comes in right when my grandson needs school fees, so I’ll keep those 2 mu for now.

The wheat went in last October with an improved variety, Jimai 22, because it stands up to our cold winters. I did rotary tillage before planting and I’ll irrigate four times total—one winter irrigation and three in spring. For fertilizer, I’ll put about 18 kg of nitrogen per mu on the wheat. The extension man says 15 kg is enough, but last year I did 18 and the crop looked stronger, so I’ll stick with that. I’ll also add about 6 kg of phosphorus and 3 kg of potassium per mu because this soil has been cropped hard for years. For pesticides, I’ll spray four times—twice for insects, once for weeds, and once for fungus when the weather turns humid.

For the summer maize, I’ll plant hybrid Denghai 605 right after the wheat comes off in early June. I buy fresh hybrid seed every year because saved seed doesn’t breed true. I’ll use no-tillage planting to save time and fuel—there’s barely a week between wheat harvest and maize planting, so I hire a custom operator with a no-till planter. I’ll give the maize about 16 kg N, 4 kg P, and 3 kg K per mu, irrigate twice around the trumpet and filling stages, and spray three times for pests and weeds. I expect about 480 kg per mu of wheat and 550 kg per mu of maize if the weather cooperates.

The cotton gets rotary tillage in April, and I’ll plant Guoxinmian. It needs about 12 kg N, 5 kg P, and 4 kg K per mu, and I’ll irrigate twice. Cotton pests are the real headache here—I'll spray about 14 times all told, mostly for bollworm. If the insects stay manageable, I’m hoping for around 260 kg per mu of seed cotton.
